content:
We have been working towards formalization of A∞ categories for mathlib: these are linear categories which relax the associativity axiom up to possibly infinitely many higher coherences (hence the name). Most commonly, these categories arise in symplectic geometry, and they are a good combinatorial proxy for geometric reasoning that is otherwise hard to formalize. Target applications of this library-in-development are Kadeishvili's theorem and its categorical analogue, as well as formalizing & computing braid group actions arising from geometry.

We would appreciate feedback on our very first PR, which just introduces graded R-linear quivers. This structure is central to everything else we do. Changes here will require many downstream changes in our project. See also this thread.

#40984 (+81/-0): add A-infinity grading data

Contributors: @Justin Mu @Annie Yao @Niels Voss

It is very difficult to say if the design of this formalization is going to be right. One of the key question-marks is how you will handle the "dependent type theory hell" aspects that are going to appear. I would suggest you clean up the code from your repository and make a larger PR which would contain the definition of A∞ categories, so that we may make suggestions, and if/when the design look good, you may split it in smaller chunks. (I am not completely sure I would be competent for reviewing this though.)

Thank you @Joël Riou, we are on to this. Without having gone through DTT hell in this case, I would expect there to be a path analogous to how the CategoryTheory library and the HomologicalComplexes library deal with the same issues. There may be some non-trivial interaction there, but so far it has been manageable.

In particular, note that our definition AInfinityPreCategory already contains all of the universe levels that matter for the category itself (which just adds the A∞ equations, and no other types). For this pre-category structure, for some universe levels u, v, w that enter our definition, we get a Type (max (max (u + 1) v) w).

I did not mention universes at all, but as you mention it: for R-linear categories in mathlib, we do not require that the types of morphisms are in the same universe as R, but it seems you do.
In https://github.com/marco-david/ainfinity-lean/blob/master/AInfinity/Stasheff.lean you are using a lot of equalities of types (which is what I was referring to by "DTT hell"). It would much more convenient to think more about how to introduce bijections (or linear equivalences?) between the corresponding types rather than using plain cast. For example, I do not think that we want a lemma like https://github.com/marco-david/ainfinity-lean/blob/f9b6e240511a889849d2be8b73079fd6371ffb65/AInfinity/Stasheff.lean#L254 in mathlib.

Another important thing is that at https://github.com/marco-david/ainfinity-lean/blob/f9b6e240511a889849d2be8b73079fd6371ffb65/AInfinity/AInfinityCategory.lean#L26 the target type of the "composition law" is a type of morphisms in a degree that is a certain integer obtained by multiple arithmetic operations, which may be what we want only up to propositional equality. Following a design like in docs#CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.comp would be more convenient IMO.
